chart_types.what: Bars comparing one value across categories
chart_types.best_for: Comparing a count or total across a bounded set of categories
chart_types.not_for: Trends over time, or shares of a whole

chart_types.what: Bars laid out sideways so long names stay readable
chart_types.best_for: Comparing categories with long labels

chart_types.what: A dot on a thin stem per category
chart_types.best_for: Comparing many categories with less ink than bars

chart_types.what: Two dots per category joined by a line
chart_types.best_for: Before and after, such as the last two runs

chart_types.what: Bars split into the parts that make them up
chart_types.best_for: Comparing totals and their parts across categories

chart_types.what: Bars normalised to 100% and split into parts
chart_types.best_for: Comparing the mix of parts across categories

chart_types.what: A value across dated, comparable runs
chart_types.best_for: Change over time between comparable runs

chart_types.what: A line with the area beneath filled
chart_types.best_for: Emphasising the size of a value over time

chart_types.what: A line that changes in steps
chart_types.best_for: Values that change at discrete moments

chart_types.what: A band from a low to a high value over time
chart_types.best_for: Ranges or uncertainty around a trend

chart_types.what: A value with its uncertainty range
chart_types.best_for: Estimates with known uncertainty

chart_types.what: Areas stacked to show how parts build a total over time
chart_types.best_for: How the parts of a total change over time

chart_types.what: Stacked areas normalised to 100%
chart_types.best_for: How the mix changes over time

chart_types.what: A tiny trend line with no axes
chart_types.best_for: A glance at direction next to a number

chart_types.what: Slices showing each category's share of a complete total
chart_types.best_for: Part-to-whole over a few complete, non-overlapping categories

chart_types.what: A pie with a hollow centre
chart_types.best_for: The same part-to-whole questions as a pie

chart_types.what: Slices whose radius also grows with value
chart_types.best_for: Not enabled in this initial catalog; radial area can exaggerate differences

chart_types.what: Sorted bars with a cumulative percentage line
chart_types.best_for: Finding the few categories that make up most of a total
chart_types.not_for: Values that do not add up

chart_types.what: A running total built from signed steps
chart_types.best_for: Explaining how a total moved between two states

chart_types.what: Stages narrowing in a declared order
chart_types.best_for: Counts that genuinely drop stage by stage

chart_types.what: Stages widening in a declared order
chart_types.best_for: Counts that genuinely grow stage by stage

chart_types.what: A 10 by 10 grid, one square per percent
chart_types.best_for: Communicating simple shares to a general audience

chart_types.what: Points placed by two measures
chart_types.best_for: How two measures relate across assets

chart_types.what: A scatter with point size as a third measure
chart_types.best_for: Relating two measures with a third as weight
chart_types.not_for: Precise reading of the third measure

chart_types.what: A scatter with a straight trend line
chart_types.best_for: Showing an overall relationship between two measures

chart_types.what: How many values fall in each range
chart_types.best_for: The spread of raw scores

chart_types.what: Median, quartiles and extremes of each group
chart_types.best_for: Comparing spreads between groups

chart_types.what: A smoothed outline of a distribution
chart_types.best_for: The shape of a large sample

chart_types.what: The share of values at or below each value
chart_types.best_for: Reading thresholds such as 'how many score under 40'

chart_types.what: Every value as a point along a line
chart_types.best_for: Small samples where each value matters

chart_types.what: Every value as a point, spread to avoid overlap
chart_types.best_for: Small samples with clusters

chart_types.what: Every pair of up to six measures as small scatters
chart_types.best_for: Exploring how several measures relate

chart_types.what: How strongly each pair of measures moves together
chart_types.best_for: Spotting related measures

chart_types.what: Each asset as a line across several measures
chart_types.best_for: Comparing profiles across many measures

chart_types.what: Profiles drawn across shared indicators
chart_types.best_for: Little here; shapes are easy to misread

chart_types.what: Bars arranged around a circle
chart_types.best_for: Cyclic categories such as hours

chart_types.what: A dial for one value against a range

chart_types.what: A value against a target and quality bands
chart_types.best_for: Progress against an agreed target

chart_types.what: A filled bar towards a maximum
chart_types.best_for: Simple progress such as task completion

chart_types.what: A coloured grid over two categories
chart_types.best_for: Counts across two categories, such as platform by score class

chart_types.what: One coloured cell per day on a calendar
chart_types.best_for: Activity per day over months

chart_types.what: Open, high, low and close per period
chart_types.best_for: Market data

chart_types.what: Decline from a running peak
chart_types.best_for: Financial series

chart_types.what: Compounded growth from periodic returns
chart_types.best_for: Financial series

chart_types.what: Tasks as bars on a timeline
chart_types.best_for: Schedules

chart_types.what: Nested rectangles sized by value
chart_types.best_for: Sizes of disjoint groups and their members

chart_types.what: Nested rings sized by value
chart_types.best_for: The same questions as a treemap, radially

chart_types.what: A rooted node-link tree
chart_types.best_for: One clear hierarchy

description.what: Bar chart of {measure_words} for each {dimension_words}, sorted largest first
description.best_for: Comparing a metric across a bounded set of categories
description.not_for: Trends over time or shares of a whole

description.what: Top {top_n} {dimension_words} by {measure_words}; {omitted} more are not charted
description.best_for: Highlighting the largest categories when there are too many to chart

description.what: Share of total {measure_words} by {dimension_words} (complete, mutually exclusive)
description.best_for: Part-to-whole questions over a complete, small set of categories

description.what: {measure_words} across dated analysis runs ({time_words})
description.best_for: Change over comparable, ordered runs

description.what: Asset-level table with recommendation status and evidence links
description.best_for: Inspecting candidates and checking which lack evidence
description.not_for: Seeing a pattern at a glance

description.what: Exact values in a sortable, accessible table
description.best_for: Precise lookup, many rows, or when no chart is faithful

description.what: This result has no rows for the current scope
description.best_for: Empty results

description.what: Horizontal bars of {measure_words} for each {dimension_words}, largest first
description.best_for: Comparing categories with long names
description.not_for: Trends over time or shares of a whole

description.what: A dot per {dimension_words} showing {measure_words}, largest first
description.best_for: Comparing a handful of categories with a light touch
description.not_for: Many categories or shares of a whole

description.what: {measure_words} by {dimension_words}, largest first, with the running share of the total
description.best_for: Finding the few categories that make up most of a total

description.what: Share of total {measure_words} by {dimension_words}, as a ring
description.best_for: Part-to-whole over a few complete, non-overlapping categories

description.what: Share of total {measure_words} by {dimension_words}, one square per percent
description.best_for: A simple share at a glance for a general audience

description.what: How many items fall in each range of {measure_words}
description.best_for: Seeing how values are spread

description.what: Median, quartiles and extremes of {measure_words}
description.best_for: Spotting the middle, the spread and outliers
description.not_for: Totals per category or tiny samples

description.what: Every item's {measure_words} as a point
description.best_for: Small samples where each item matters

description.what: Every item's {measure_words} as a point, spread out to stay visible
description.best_for: Small samples with clusters

description.what: The share of items at or below each value of {measure_words}
description.best_for: Reading thresholds, such as how many items score under 40

description.what: A smoothed outline of how {measure_words} is spread
description.best_for: The overall shape of a larger sample
description.not_for: Small samples, where the curve looks surer than the data

description.what: Bar chart of {measure_words} for each {dimension_words}, in its declared order
description.best_for: Counts across an ordered scale, such as low, medium, high
description.not_for: Named categories with no natural order

description.what: {measure_words} across dated, comparable runs ({time_words}), area filled
description.best_for: Emphasising how large a value is over time

description.what: {measure_words} across dated, comparable runs ({time_words}), in steps
description.best_for: Values that change only when a run happens

description.what: A small trend of {measure_words} across runs, without axes
description.best_for: A glance at direction

description.what: {measure_words} across comparable runs, stacked by {series_words}
description.best_for: How the parts of a total change between runs
description.not_for: Parts that overlap or can be negative

description.what: Share of {measure_words} by {series_words} across comparable runs (each run is 100%)
description.best_for: How the mix changes between runs

description.what: {measure_words} for each {dimension_words}, split by {series_words}
description.best_for: Comparing totals and their parts across categories
description.not_for: Parts that overlap or can be negative

description.what: Mix of {series_words} within each {dimension_words} (each bar is 100%)
description.best_for: Comparing the mix across categories of different size

description.what: {measure_words} for every {dimension_words} and {series_words}, as a coloured grid
description.best_for: Spotting where counts concentrate across two categories
description.not_for: Reading exact values; the table has them

description.what: Network of {source_words} and {target_words}, each link labelled with what it means
description.best_for: Seeing which assets are related, and how
description.not_for: Reading amounts; the table has the exact values

description.what: {measure_words} flowing from {source_words} to {target_words}, ribbons sized by amount
description.best_for: Real quantities moving between stages
description.not_for: Similarity or dependency, which do not flow

description.what: {measure_words} in each {target_words}, as nested rectangles
description.best_for: Comparing the size of disjoint groups and their members
description.not_for: Members in more than one group

description.what: {measure_words} in each {target_words}, as nested rings
description.best_for: The same question as a treemap, drawn radially
description.not_for: Members in more than one group

description.what: The members of one {target_words}, as a tree
description.best_for: Seeing what one group contains
